title: Prefill-aware kernel composer with latency regret tracker
creator: Aisha Gomez
description: Design and implement a prefill-aware kernel composition layer and accompanying online latency regret tracker to reduce tail latency and token cost. Instead of a single static kernel selector, the kernel composer composes microkernels across prefill and decode phases and dynamically switches based on a lightweight latency predictor and short exploratory trials. The goal is to make kernel selection sensitive to architecture (SM compute capability, tile sizes), workload seqlen distribution (prefill-heavy vs decode-heavy), KV-cache hit rates, and current queueing, while maintaining safety for high-SLA customers via guarded fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: Composer returns per-request kernel plan (prefill kernel + decode kernel) within 1ms median decision time in production path
Online regret tracker shows decreasing cumulative regret compared to baseline static selector across 2 weeks of traffic
95th percentile token latency reduced by >=10% in canary region for at least two benchmarked workloads
Unit-cost (tokens/$) reduced by >=5% for mixed short/long seqlen synthetic workload in A/B experiment
Rollout plan with automatic fallback to 'stable-kernel' exists and has been tested with failover chaos test
tasks: Define kernel fingerprint vector (arch features, tile sizes, flop efficiency, kernel memory pressure)
Implement lightweight latency predictor trained from microbenchmarks + online corrections
Build bandit controller (Thompson Sampling + temperature decay softmax) for short-run trials
Integrate prefilling-aware policy that chooses a separate kernel for prefill vs decode and a transition point
Add cumulative regret metric and dashboard in Console; emit token-level telemetry for offline analysis
Canary rollout and controlled A/B experiment with rollback hooks
updates: 2025-02-10: Ticket created after spike in tail latency for models with mixed long prefill and short decode patterns.
2025-02-15: Experiment design sketched; decided on two-stage approach: offline warmstart + online microtrials.
2025-02-20: Latency predictor prototype implemented (RidgeRegression on microbenchmark features). Initial MAE ~0.24ms on holdout set.
2025-02-24: Bandit controller implemented; deployed to dev cluster with synthetic traffic. Early results show exploration converges in ~300 requests per model fingerprint.
2025-02-28: Integrated composer into prefill path; decision latency optimized to 0.9ms median after caching fingerprint lookups.
2025-03-01: Canary started in us-west-2 on low-traffic slice; observing 12% reduction in 95p latency for conversational benchmark A, cost neutral so far. Monitoring for regressions.
experiment_results: Synthetic-mix-1 (50% prefill>1024, 50% decode<64): 95p latency -10.8%, cost -6.1% (canary), sample size 48k requests
Conv-benchmark-A (production canary): 95p latency -12.3%, 99p latency -5.1%, observed kv-cache warmstart improved accuracy of predictor
Edge-case long-seqlen-only workload: composer chose single high-throughput kernel for both phases; no regression observed
rollout_plan: Week 0: dev + staging integration; Week 1: canary in us-west-2 on 1% traffic slice; Week 2: expand to 10% if no regressions (monitor 99p latency, error rates); Week 3: global rollout with per-customer opt-out and SLA guards. Automatic rollback if 99p latency increases >7% or error rate increases >0.1%.
risks: Incorrect predictor bias under unseen hardware causing poor kernel choices; mitigated by fallback to stable kernel and offline warmstart
Exploration-induced jitter for latency-sensitive customers; mitigated by traffic-sliced microtrials and conservative exploration schedule
Telemetry volume increase; mitigated by sampling and on-demand detailed traces
next_steps: Add GPU sm/mem pressure features to fingerprint and retrain predictor with extended microbenchmarks
Automate weekly offline tuner job (Bayesian optimization) to update prior for online bandit
Add per-customer policy flags to disable online exploration and enforce deterministic selection
